note_sections.t: Return to urology clinic for treatment decision regarding known prostate adenocarcinoma following recent biopsy confirmation.

Mechanical engineer, currently living with his unmarried partner and adult child in a multi-generational household. He is a non-smoker, abstains from alcohol, and cycles approximately 20 km twice weekly. His only significant medical history is chronic kidney disease with baseline creatinine 157 umol/L and eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m2. He reports mild lower urinary tract symptoms (IPSS 4/35) without nocturia or urgency. Recently evaluated at the sleep clinic for suspected obstructive sleep apnoea. He has no history of cardiovascular disease or diabetes mellitus.

On digital rectal examination, a firm nodule is palpable in the right peripheral zone apex, consistent with clinical stage cT2a. The prostate is non-tender and approximately 27 mL in volume. General examination reveals a well-nourished male with stable vital signs, BP 127/74 mmHg, HR 65 bpm, and no signs of peripheral edema or lymphadenopathy.
